title: Singular Matrices and the Equivalence List
quickIdea: For a square matrix, singular, determinant zero, not invertible, rank below n, dependent rows and a zero eigenvalue are six names for one condition.
remember: A square matrix A is singular when |A| = 0 and non-singular when |A| is not 0.

For an n x n A these are all equivalent: |A| = 0; rank(A) < n; A has no inverse; the rows are linearly dependent; the columns are linearly dependent; 0 is an eigenvalue; Ax = 0 has a non-zero solution.
A product u v^T of a non-zero column and a non-zero row has rank 1, so for n at least 2 it is singular however large its entries are.
The sum of two singular matrices can be non-singular, and the sum of two non-singular matrices can be singular: [[1,0],[0,0]] + [[0,0],[0,1]] = I_2, and I_2 + (-I_2) = O.
det(A + B) is unrelated to det(A) + det(B) in either direction, so no conclusion about A can be drawn from det(A + B) = det(B) alone.

example.prompt: A is the product of the column [[2],[-4],[7]] with the row [[1,9,5]]. Find |A| without computing all nine entries.
example.work: The product is 3 x 3 and every row is a multiple of (1,9,5), namely 2 times it, -4 times it and 7 times it, so the rows are dependent and the determinant is 0. Equivalently A = u v^T has rank 1, which is below 3.
example.answer: |A| = 0. This is GATE CSE 2014 Set 2 Q.4.

gateAngle: GATE CSE 2014 Set 2 Q.4 is this one-line argument, and GATE CSE 2020 Q.27 tests whether you know that the sum of two singular matrices may be non-singular while det(A + B) has no law.

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: Give two singular 2 x 2 matrices whose sum is non-singular.
variations.why: Each has determinant 0, and the sum is the identity with determinant 1, so singularity is not preserved by addition.

variations.label: CONCEPTUAL PRACTICE QUESTION
variations.question: Why does a zero eigenvalue make a matrix singular?
variations.answer: Av = 0 with v non-zero means A sends a non-zero vector to zero, so A cannot be inverted; equivalently the columns are dependent and |A| = 0.
variations.why: A zero eigenvalue is exactly the existence of a non-zero vector in the null space.

variations.label: PREDICTED VARIATION
variations.question: A is 5 x 5 with rank(A) = 3. Is A invertible, and how many of its eigenvalues must be 0?
variations.answer: Not invertible, and at least two eigenvalues are 0.
variations.why: The nullity is 5 - 3 = 2, and every null vector is an eigenvector for the eigenvalue 0, so 0 has geometric multiplicity at least 2.

trap.what: Concluding that a matrix with no zero entries is non-singular, or that det(A) = 0 follows from det(A + B) = det(B).
trap.why: Determinant zero is a statement about linear dependence, not about how many zero entries appear, and the determinant is not additive.
trap.counterexample: [[1,2],[2,4]] has no zero entry and determinant 0, while [[0,1],[1,0]] has two zero entries and determinant -1.

check.question: A is 3 x 3 with rank 2. What is |A|?
check.explanation: rank < 3 means the three rows are dependent, and a dependent set of n rows in an n x n matrix forces the determinant to vanish.
